Applies to this screen and the Fast note dialog. Widget card colours are set separately.
The file will be deleted. There is no trash in the app to recover it from, and if the folder is synced the deletion will follow to your other devices.

Something broken, or just using it?
Say hi — tell me you use it
Only needed if your notes folder is not the top of your vault. Without it, tapping a note may open the wrong one, and a .git folder one level up stays invisible.
Helps find crashes and shows how many people use the app. Off until you say otherwise. It is written not to include note contents, file names or folder paths.
The widget can show a small chip telling you when your notes last synced, so you notice when syncing quietly stops.
Reads .git left behind by whatever client you use — GitSync, Obsidian Git, Termux. The app does not run git itself and does not write to it.
No sync tool exposes its state in the folder, so the chip shows when a note last changed. That is enough to notice a sync that died.
The chip turns amber. Match it to how often your git client runs — with a 15-minute schedule, a whole quiet day already means something broke.
No .md files in this folder yet. Create a note with the + button on the widget, then come back and pick it here.
This app is made by one person in their spare time. Bug reports are read, and knowing someone out there uses it is what keeps it going.
Obsidian vault \"%1$s\" detected, so tapping a note on the widget opens the right file. Nothing to set up here.
No .git folder here — that is fine if you sync another way. If you do use Obsidian Git, pick the folder that contains .git, usually one level above your notes.
Found .git but could not read it: %1$s
Unfinished merge (MERGE_HEAD present) — most likely a conflict waiting in your git client.
A rebase was started and never finished — resolve it in your git client.
Local branch differs from origin — changes are waiting to be pushed or pulled.
Crash reports show me what breaks, and usage numbers show how many people the app is for. They never include your notes, their names or your folder paths. You can change this later in settings.
Tapping a note on the widget opens it here.
A deep link into Obsidian. Needs the vault to be worked out correctly, which the app does for you.
Hands the file to whatever you have set for Markdown. Works with any editor, and it can save back to the same file.
Android asks which app to use each time.
